Earthshot Prize Awards’ Impact Assembly was held in Mumbai on November 16, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement
Global giants including Amazon, NVIDIA, Uber, and IKEA among others joined forces with Earthshot Prize winners and finalists at the ‘Impact Assembly’ in Mumbai on Monday (November 16, 2026) to announce a wave of new partnerships, investments, and expansions to scale environmental solutions.
The announcements at the Prize’s Impact Assembly — aimed at bringing together environmental innovators, business leaders, philanthropists and government representatives — could lead to hundreds of millions of people around the world breathing cleaner air, being better protected from extreme weather, and benefiting from a more stable climate, the organisers said in a statement.
Mumbai will host the sixth annual Earthshot Prize Awards on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), with Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, attending the ceremony. The event will recognise five winners from among 15 finalists developing solutions to some of the world’s most pressing environmental challenges.
“Over the past six years, Earthshot has shown me that the people with the answers are already out there. Our task is to find them, back them and help them scale. So I ask everyone here to support these Finalists. Give them your ideas, your influence and your investment. Help them take their solutions to the world,” said Prince William, the founder and President of The Earthshot Prize.
Among the major announcements at the Impact Assembly, 2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Pula (Fix Our Climate) announced that it has secured new partnerships with two of the world’s leading technology companies, putting it on course to quadruple the number of smallholder farmers it protects from extreme weather to 100 million by 2030.
Amazon announced a commitment to cover the full cost of Pula’s cloud credits through to 2030. “It will also give Pula new climate data, technical expertise and access to its vast partner network, which will strengthen the platform as it grows,” the official release said.
Further, Pula also said that it is joining the NVIDIA Inception programme, which will allow it to use NVIDIA Earth-2 — an AI platform for weather and climate. “It produces far more detailed forecasts than traditional models and does so at much greater speed. With Earth-2’s advanced modelling, Pula will be able to see more clearly how drought and extreme weather will affect the farmers it serves.” the statement added.
The State of Gujarat (Clean Our Air), which is the 2025 Earthshot Prize Finalist, has pioneered the world’s first trading scheme to cut harmful particle pollution from factories. At the Impact Assembly this time, it said it will — through its partner the Emissions Market Accelerator — expand the model to more Indian States, potentially benefiting a further 210 million people.
“The scale-ups, first in Maharashtra and followed by work in Rajasthan, let industry grow while giving people cleaner, healthier air to breathe. The scheme sets a limit on how much pollution factories can release in total. Factories that cut their pollution can sell their unused allowance to others, which rewards businesses for cleaning up,” the release stated.
2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Mahila Housing Trust (Fix Our Climate) announced that it would launch a world-first, to protect a further 1,00,000 women in low-income communities across Asia from extreme heat, and a world-first insurance scheme for pregnant women. “It pays at lower temperatures than standard policies, and philanthropic funding tops up the payouts so expectant mothers can afford to rest on the hottest days. Throughout pregnancy, women also get access to cooling, medical care, heatwave warnings and health advice.”
In India, The Trust said it is moving into Nabha in Punjab and Bikaner in Rajasthan. “There it will help local governments plan for extreme heat and install 50,000 cool roofs, coated with reflective paint that keeps homes up to five degrees cooler,” it added.
Another significant announcement was the 2022 Earthshot Prize Finalist Phool (Build a Waste-Free World) unveiling $6 million dollar in new debt financing from three major Indian banks: the Export-Import Bank of India (Exim), the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) and ICICI Bank. “The deal shows that circular-economy solutions are winning the backing of mainstream finance,” it said.
‘Phool’ turns temple flowers that would otherwise be dumped in rivers and landfill into a leather alternative that is free of animal products and plastic. “Since 2022, it has grown from processing 36 tonnes of flowers a day in two Indian states to 50 tonnes a day across four.”
Other partnership announcements included — 2021 Earthshot Prize Finalist SOLshare (Fix Our Climate) unveiling that it has signed $20 million dollar in new solar energy deals through its Greener Garments Initiative; 2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Mother Earth Foundation (Build a Waste-Free World) announcing that it is bringing its community-led waste schemes to six more cities and provinces in the Philippines; 2026 Earthshot Prize Finalist Satellites on Fire (Clean Our Air) revealing an expansion of its AI-powered wildfire detection to Brazil and Panama; 2025 Finalist Matter (Revive Our Oceans) delivering its first solution designed to capture microfibres from wastewater at an IKEA textile supplier in India.
“Together, these major breakthroughs show how investment, partnerships and expansions are helping proven environmental solutions reach more people and places around the world and change entire systems for the better,” the Earthshot Prize said in its official release.
